title: Professor Nickerson, New Orleans piano teacher
summary: William Nickerson as a classic teacher, his daughter at Wilberforce, his fees and home, and Jelly's lessons.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: I know John played trumpet. See, he was on the cold weather side with me. For a while, I was glad he met yesterday, too. Did you ever get any data on William Nicholson? Professor Nicholson?
No, except the fastest over there. He studied piano with him for a while.

Well, he, somewhere, I don't know if you want to cut it off. No, it's all right. He was actually one of the real classic teachers in the audience. That's what Festus did. And his daughter is now Dean of the Department of Music at Wilberforce University. Is that the... Camille Nicholson. That's the daughter of the old professor. That's the daughter of the father. She's an old woman now, for that matter. How much is that now? No. He was... How much is that now? She's at Wilberforce. Huh? She's at Wilberforce in Ohio. Dean of the Department of Music. And she's also... She was president of the Negro Music Teachers Association. I think she's a... She's a vice president or a president emeritus. She is a very, very fine musician. And of course, old man Nicholson was a mighty fine musician. He taught the piano and the violin. Man, he could tell you more about it than my... He took us... Clean... The gal would come out. He's the one that raised the price on music teaching in New Orleans. You couldn't come to him for no 50 cents, no a dollar even. Two. Hmm. One. One. My price. My price. My attorney manual for... $15,000. No, you could come along and... It was way back though, yeah. Yeah. You didn't know him until about 19... 19 or so. I never met him until 1920. I went out to his house to see what he arranged a number for me. He won $25. What is it, Galvis Canal? Yeah. He was off... Off Canal. He was by Galvis and... He was on Galvis. He was between Galvis and Denver. Yeah, that's right. Uh... Iberville. Yeah, Galvis and... Off of Iberville.
You must have studied with him back in 1905 or before, wasn't it, D-Fat? Yeah, he was. You remember when he was teaching me with? Huh?

He was at University. Yeah. I don't remember when he was there. See, when I... He was... He was Professor there. Yeah. When I was at your University. Yeah. Well, I remember... Professor Mamba. Huh? My remembrance of him is just after I got to New Orleans. Oh, yeah. But I had read of it being the orchestra lead on the original Georgia Ministers. And the days when W.C. Handy led the Georgia Ministers band. And that was long before my time. Oh, yeah.
Well, we were talking about... Now, Jelly Roll took some lessons from Professor Nickerson, too. He told... Oh, yeah.
Oh, yeah. I recall in his LP where he used to talk about this woman who used to take lessons from. See, every tune she played was the same thing. Oh, yeah.
Yeah. Some woman that was teaching him. Yeah. It's come to find out she couldn't read one note. Yeah.
